raw_text:
This study aims to investigate the reasons behind the inconsistency in completion times for sites employing the same nominal work process. Understanding the measurable factors contributing to these differences is paramount, as they can inform improvements in process efficiency and productivity. The study will identify potential explanations for the variations and design an empirical study to distinguish these explanations.

Assumptions
- Work processes are standardized across sites.
- Completion times vary despite standardized processes.
- Differences in completion times can be attributed to measurable factors.
- Bayesian methods provide a suitable framework for analyzing this study.

Research design
The research will employ a Bayesian methodological approach. Bayesian methods allow for the incorporation of prior knowledge into the analysis of data while examining the impact of varying factors on completion times. By utilizing a Bayesian approach, the study can update its understanding of the factors influencing completion times as more data becomes available.

Data or evidence needed
- Completion times for all operational sites involved in the same nominal work process.
- Standardized work process documentation and performance metrics.
- Any available historical data on work process variations or deviations from the standard.
- Data on time spent on various stages of the work process, such as setup, processing, and inspection phases.

Measurement
- Completion times should be measured by an objective method, such as stopwatches or automated timestamps.
- The standardized work process will be measured through observations and process documentation.
- Time spent on each stage of the work process will be recorded through methodical observations.

Analysis
- Bayesian hierarchical models will be used to estimate the relationships between the relevant variables.
- Prior knowledge about work process elements will be incorporated into the model.
- Quantify the impact of potential explanatory factors on completion times and probability distributions.

Decision / stopping rule
The study will continue until the Bayesian model converges, providing a stable and reliable estimate of the relationships between variables. If convergence is not achieved after several iterations, the dataset may be reconsidered to correct inconsistencies or missing data.

Limitations
- The assumption that all sites follow the standardized work process may not hold.
- The data collection process may introduce biases or inaccuracies.
- The study's ability to capture all relevant factors may be limited by available data or observations.
